svg.title: TOPAK H3 — Verification map: what is checked, what must fail, and what the checks do not claim
svg.desc: Every check in the corpus: seventeen TLA+ modules run in TLC at small constants, each property with a mutation that must fail and a reachability witness that must be violated; the policy floor's gates with a pinned proof checker; the reference's tests restating the properties; the trace harness that replays those tests through an operational model; the drift pins; and the lineage gate suite. Then the honesty layer: these are evidence, not proofs, and what runs is not what is checked.

text.tspan: Drift: records and modules pinned by the reference
: what it checks, what must fail, and where its result is

svg.text: Seventeen modules (G7 §9). Properties are invariants checked under Mut = "none"; each mutation changes the mechanism, never the property, and must produce a counterexample; each Never… witness must be violated, which shows the behaviour it names is reachable. Results files are hand-assembled TLC output with a dated name and never change. Pinned means listed in mechanism/corpus-pins.sha256.

svg.text: Since 2026.09.30 the restatement is checked, not asserted, on every path a test takes: each state these tests build records its applied entries and spec/mechanism-trace-run.sh replays them through Mechanism.tla. Nothing a test does not reach is checked. The same kind of evidence the TLA+ runs are, by the same hand.

text.tspan: 5 · The honesty layer: what none of the above claims

svg.text: "No theorem is proved." The TLA+ artifacts discriminate and check non-vacuity at small constants; the trace validation is drift detection against a model of the
code; a checked proof certifies an implication between two Cedar encodings, not the encoding (G7 §8; spec/README).
The theorem-to-premise table says what each check assumed; it does not strengthen the check.
"A property that holds at two principals and one epoch is evidence, not a proof" (T-0045-29, G5 §8). The constants are printed in each results file: MaxEpoch = 1
TLC itself is a trust-root row: "no error has been found" is taken to mean what it says.
Every record, run and ratification of 2026.10.01 was made by the person who ratified it, or drafted at that person's request, on the day; the wrapper and the
controls that test it are the same hand's (G7 §8).
The operational model was written from the code by the same hand on the same day: the link is mechanized, not independent (ADR-0033 A5).

text.tspan: What runs is not what is checked

svg.text: "What runs is not the specification" (ADR-0045 §5, R1): no refinement from the modules to the Rust exists, TLC runs at small constants, the build is asserted and
not reproduced. Each is a trust-root row, T-0045-28 to 30, for every deployment.
"The gap is a debt, not a residual the archetype keeps" (R2): its owner is ADR-0033.

text.tspan: What the checker does not cover

svg.text: A holds° is cedar's own term folding with no query to check: 25 of the run's 29 holds rest on the engine's row (T-0045-3), not the checker's (G7 item 69).
The CPC signature is cvc5's own formalization, trusted as written; the three lying-solver controls test the wrapper's refusals, not the signature's rules (G7 §4).
Stage 1, trace validation: A5 (Batch 21), rerun at A6. Stage 2, a Lean model with differential testing, and stage 3, its compilation: "the chain proper", not begun.
The reproducible build (T-0045-30) is untouched. Each addendum says which stage it discharges, and the rows leave Annex A only on that addendum.
